results.content: ![Image 3: Health AI in 2026: CU Researchers are Implementing Trustworthy Tools to Support Clinicians](https://news.cuanschutz.edu/hubfs/health_ai_2026_llms_yanjun_gao.png). Researchers in the [Department of Biomedical Informatics](https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/dbmi) (DBMI) at the [University of Colorado Anschutz](https://www.cuanschutz.edu/) (CU Anschutz) are leveraging LLMs to improve healthcare—seeking to improve the experience of both patients and clinicians. For example, [LLMs are being used to summarize the electronic health records (EHRs) of patients to save time for clinicians](https://news.cuanschutz.edu/dbmi/evaluating-ai-in-clinical-summarization). [Yanjun Gao](https://som.cuanschutz.edu/Profiles/Faculty/Profile/39558), PhD, assistant professor of [biomedical informatics](https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/dbmi) at CU Anschutz, thinks the answer is more nuanced than a simple “yes” or “no.” Gao and her team in the [Language, Reasoning, and Knowledge Lab](https://www.larknlp.com/) (LARK Lab) are researching how these tools can be effectively deployed in medical settings. results.title: Evaluation of large language models on mental health - Frontiers
results.content: # Evaluation of large language models on mental health: from knowledge test to illness diagnosis. This study systematically evaluates 15 state-of-the-art LLMs, including DeepSeekR1/V3 (March 24, 2025), GPT-4.1 (April 15, 2025), Llama4 (April 5, 2025), and QwQ (March 6, 2025, developed by Alibaba), on two key tasks: mental health knowledge testing and mental illness diagnosis in the Chinese context. Additionally, most of the studies focused on a single aspect when assessing the applicability of LLMs in mental health, such as evaluating the model’s conversational abilities or text generation quality. This study systematically evaluates the performance of state-of-the-art LLMs, including DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4.1, and QwQ, across two critical tasks in the mental health domain: mental health knowledge assessment and mental illness diagnosis. Keywords: large language models, model evaluation, mental health, knowledge test, illness diagnosis. Citation: Xu Y, Fang Z, Lin W, Jiang Y, Jin W, Balaji P, Wang J and Xia T (2025) Evaluation of large language models on mental health: from knowledge test to illness diagnosis.
